security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown backticks, reporting guidance, or fixed git status calls. One high-risk finding is confirmed because scripts/run_command.py executes a user-supplied command in a target repository. No prompt injection or additional semantic intent issue was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.suggestion: Require an explicit user confirmation before running the selected command, and keep shell execution disabled.
Add an optional allowlist or dry-run mode for documented smoke, inference, evaluation, and sanity commands.
Document that captured stdout and stderr should be reviewed before sharing reproduction reports.

content.user_title: Run Reproduction Commands and Audit Results
content.value_statement: Reproduction work needs clear evidence from a selected command. This skill runs a short documented command and writes standardized output files.
actual_capabilities: Runs a selected command in a target repository with a configurable timeout.
Captures stdout, stderr, return code, timeout state, and launch errors.
Records git status before and after the command to identify touched files.
Parses simple numeric metrics from command output.
Classifies runs as success, partial, or blocked for reporting.
Provides a wrapper for standardized repro_outputs reporting bundles.
limitations: It does not choose the reproduction target or setup plan.
It is not intended for training, resume, or long-running jobs.
The selected command can still perform unsafe local actions.
Metric parsing only handles simple numeric name-value patterns.

use_cases.title: Verify a Repository Smoke Test
use_cases.description: Run the documented smoke command and produce clear evidence for a reproduction report.

use_cases.title: Capture an Evaluation Attempt
use_cases.description: Record an inference or evaluation run after setup decisions are already made.

use_cases.title: Review Reproduction Evidence
use_cases.description: Compare command output, exit status, metrics, and file changes in a standardized bundle.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Basic Smoke Check
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner check with a known repository command.
prompt_templates.prompt: Run the selected smoke command for this repository with a 60 second timeout. Capture stdout, stderr, status, and changed files.

prompt_templates.title: Normalize Existing Evidence
prompt_templates.scenario: Convert captured run evidence into standard outputs.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use existing execution evidence for the selected command and write the standard reproduction outputs. Separate verified facts from assumptions.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Patch Impact
prompt_templates.scenario: Check whether a run changed repository files.
prompt_templates.prompt: Run the documented evaluation command, capture before and after git status, and summarize any files changed by the run.

prompt_templates.title: Classify a Failed Run
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced audit after a blocked or partial run.
prompt_templates.prompt: Run the selected inference command with a defined timeout. If it fails, classify the blocker, metrics, touched paths, and next validation step.

output_examples.input: Selected command exits successfully and reports accuracy equals 0.82.
output: Report notes no blocker and lists captured command output.

output_examples.input: Selected command times out after the configured limit.
output_examples.output: Status: partial. Main blocker: command did not finish within the timeout. Monitoring scope records the timeout value.

output_examples.input: Selected command fails because the executable is missing.
output_examples.output: Status: blocked. The report explains the missing executable and keeps stdout and stderr separate.

best_practices: Use a command documented by the repository or selected by the user.
Set a short timeout before running inference, evaluation, smoke, or sanity checks.
Review captured logs before sharing them, because command output may contain sensitive paths or tokens.
anti_patterns: Do not use this skill to choose the research target or design the setup plan.
Do not start training jobs, resumes, or long-running processes through this workflow.
Do not treat a partial run as verified success.

faq.question: Does this skill choose which command to run?
faq.answer: No. It expects a selected command and focuses on execution evidence and reporting.

faq.question: Can it run training?
faq.answer: No. It is scoped to short non-training smoke, inference, evaluation, or sanity commands.

faq.question: What output files does it support?
faq.answer: It supports standardized reproduction outputs such as summaries, command records, logs, status data, and patch notes.

faq.question: Does it modify repository files?
faq.answer: The runner records evidence. The selected command may change files, so the skill captures before and after git status.

faq.question: How are metrics detected?
faq.answer: It parses simple numeric name-value patterns from stdout and stderr, then reports an observed metric when available.

faq.question: Is command execution safe?
faq.answer: It avoids shell execution, captures output, and uses timeouts. Users should still review commands before running them.
